items.title: Three equivalent forms of regularity for a sequence that does not generate the unit ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a sequence which does not generate the unit ideal, regularity of every permutation, of every subsequence and of the sequence multiplied by the variables in the polynomial ring are equivalent (statement lines 17013-17024). The proof does not use the Koszul complex: it reduces to the two-element case by identifying two kernels, runs an induction on the length for the permutation statement, and then transfers regularity to the polynomial ring by checking each element on the relevant quotient (proof lines 17026-17061). The kernel identification in the two-element case is the step that starts the induction. H2.
